items.note: Story 1: the Larrow Valley Cooperative Creamery Association, organized 1889. Gideon Vose and the 1891 creamery are missing from Section A, but the item bolds four elements with no REQUIRED line, so it is scored on the core fact.
Section A says patrons were paid 'by butterfat test, not by weight of milk' but never says the test of the station where he delivers governs, and Article VII is not named.
Story 1: under payment by test this one faulty glassware determined every farmer's income, as opposed to payment by weight.
Effie Loomis, Wilbur Teague as bookkeeper and Hobart Sill as buttermaker are not identified in Section A (Teague appears only as a source citation).
Section A names Selby Vose only as manager. It gives neither son of Gideon nor 1913; B3/D3 later say 1911.
The station-gain ledger line does not appear in Section A.
Ostrey Hollow station built 1895-96 and opened 4 May 1896. The borrowed Larrow Green glass is missing, but the item has no REQUIRED line, so it is scored on the core fact.
Section A does not describe weighing, composite samples, reading the neck after a fixed pipette charge, or the cream and skim flow.
Ammon & Sons, Tarnet; invoice 14 April 1897; in use 1 May 1897.
Six dozen pipettes marked 17.6 c.c., 12 dozen bottles, acid measure, hand tester, freight, $77.93.
Story 2: 0.19 in every month, wet February and dry June alike, year after year. The run mislabels it as the gap to the valley average, which is penalized at A4.3.
Section A does not say the pipette cannot be checked without a burette or that the county had none.
Keddie tester from the 4 May 1896 opening; dismissed 30 April 1925 after twenty-nine seasons.
Section A does not describe the test book's columns or its crossed-and-initialed corrections.
Section A has no summary leaf and no 1896 figure of 3.80. It gives 3.61 only as the Hollow average, with no step at the glassware change.

Story 3: broke 8 May, borrowed measure to 10 July, nine weeks, tests rose then fell back, question mark. The 3.80 figure is missing, but the item has no REQUIRED line, so it is scored on the core fact. The lender attribution is penalized under A06.
Orra is Ansel's wife and Emmet's sister, and Emmet is the largest patron on the bottom (Stories 2 and 4).
The 1919 circular is present. Keddie's own 17 March 1925 statement ('tested as he was taught... cannot say why') is not; the only 'tested as taught' line is Ivy's 1958 quote.
Story 7: died 1934 with the imputation on him.
Six farms on Hessel Bottom, a wet meadow; Emmet the largest patron.
The weigh book appears only as an exhibit. There is no 1 January 1897 start and no statement that the two scales agreed.
The 1902 complaints are present, but the run gives the Hollow-vs-Green gap as 0.19 (Story 2; C1b '3.61 + 0.19'; E contradiction 2 rejects 0.17 for 0.19). The key forfeits the item for this.
The run says the committee visited 'multiple times throughout 1908'. The key has January to March only (planted error F096).
Brant's 1910 figures and the proportional loss do not appear in Section A (only in C2).
The weigh book's passage to Roy in 1929 and its loan to Ivy in 1958 are absent.
No reconstruction mentions Alder Corners, Redlow Ridge, Vessey County or Jerome Cudd.
Section A does not mention the four patrons hauling to Alder Corners from 1915.
Section A does not state that the Alder Corners test was independent.
The 0.19-higher result over sixteen seasons is not in Section A.
The same-milk, two-buildings disposal of the rival theories is not in Section A.
Rosalie Cudd appears only in Section F.
Strawn is named as Ordell circuit inspector, but the 1907-1936 span is missing from Section A (F says 'from 1908').
The lactometer and the fact that he never found water are absent from Section A.
Story 5: 12 June 1923, burette, whole lot condemned.
The run says only that he 'drew no inference'. It does not say he wrote no figure for the deficiency or made no report beyond the condemnation.
The run gives the post-condemnation average as 3.85 (key: 3.80); the 28 June and 2 July dates are also missing.
The crate going to the loft is present. The notebooks' route to the college library in 1947 is missing, and both bolded elements are required.
Petition in January 1925.
Frick; 17 March to 4 May 1925; two sessions in the station weigh room. The run says four sessions, but 'three sessions' is unbolded.
Watering (manager), theft (an Association officer) and bog hay were all argued; the award was made without admission of any cause.
Four documents including Strawn's notebook for the condemnation year, which nobody laid beside the test book.

The $3,800 award without admission, charged to the station account, is correct. The dismissal without a finding against him (this item's own aspect beyond A3.1) is not stated; the run says only 'no exoneration'.
Story 8 gives the loss as $19,600, not $19,000, and does not link the award to the station-gain account.
Story 8 calls Ivy 'Ansel's great-niece'; the key says granddaughter.
Section A does not describe her assembling the separate record series.
February 1958 in the loft is correct, but the run says eleven pipettes survived; the key says nine.
The run gives a mean of 16.27 c.c.; the key has 16.72, short 0.88 = 0.95 of the mark.
There is no 95 percent. The run's ratio is 92.4%, with a muddled '0.2 points... became 0.19'.
Section A has no 40M/76,000 lb/ledger identity; it gives $19,600.
Bulletin 471, October 1958; 24 years after his death; 35 years since condemnation.
Granddaughter.
Derived correctly: Ivy is Duncan's daughter and Duncan is Ansel's son; supported by r18 and r22's correction.
Second cousins, as children of the first cousins Roy and Duncan, with the derivation.
A08: the run never raises the full-vs-half-sibling question; its 'left open' concerns personal dynamics.
Gideon Vose, his father.
States that the payment-by-test system was Gideon's creation and that Selby, his son, signed the circular accusing the patrons.
A01 is asserted: 'there was no connection... had no foundation in fact.'
The run treats Duncan's denial as authoritative rather than noting that no document settles it.
The run gives 16.27/17.6 = 0.9244 (7.56% short); the key has 0.95, 5%.
3.80 true and 0.19 short, which match the key's values; the run got them by adding the Hollow-vs-Green gap, not by dividing by 0.95.
The run gives 80,000 lb; its 40M x 0.0361 is miscomputed as 1,440,000. Key: 76,000.
The run gives $20,000 and then 3,800/19,600 = 19.4%; the key has $19,000 and one fifth.
The run adds 0.19 to get 3.61, 7,220 and 380 lb; the key has 3.60, 7,200 and 360.
The run gives $95 (380 x 0.25); the key has $86.40.
The run gives 1,440,000; the key has 1,444,000.
The run gives 80,000, calls it '5.26% of the butterfat actually present' (NT-20) and 5.56% of credited.
72 pipettes is correct, but the run gives the shortfall as 1.33 c.c.; the key has 0.88.
The run says '26 years and one month', which is not an exact equivalent of 26 years 6 weeks, and gives 'approximately 25 years'.
A02 is asserted: 'approximately 1,100,000 lbs' (misplaced to 1897-98).
The variable is the measure: own measure broken 8 May, borrowed until 10 July.
Held constant: same tester, herds, pasture and season, scales.
The result is given only as 'markedly higher' and 'former level', with no 3.80 or 3.61.
Says the cause is the glass, not the milk or farms, and states a limit (the defect is not quantified in c.c.).
Only two valid reasons (the 1911 interval and the cream arriving heavy); the third, the 1908 committee's observation, is not a valid defeater.
Argues the reasons are independent and names the 1911 interval as surviving without the 1958 measurement.
A09 is asserted: 'Did the bookkeeper ever question...? No.'
Yes, he knew the station tested low; cites the 1919 circular.
Three elements: signed the ledger sheets with the station-gain line, wrote the 1919 circular, argued watering at the 1925 hearing (F).

No declared inability to settle whether he knew the tests were understated, and none of the supporting observations; 'another question' is not an abstention. Not deducted: the headline verdict answers the literal question.

Three correctly resolved conflicts with methods: condemnation year 1921/1922 vs 12 June 1923 (catalogued); Hazel and Ivy 'first cousin once removed' vs second cousins, by derivation; Selby as nephew vs son, by Duncan's statement.
NT-18 counts: great-niece carried by both r19 and r22, resolved by r18 and r22's own correction. The 67,000 pair is identified but not broken (the run lands on 80,000); no other pairs are found.
A04 is asserted (mold reground, manufacturing defect) and A06 is asserted (the measure borrowed from the state); A10 is not addressed.
None of the keyed self-refutations is identified; the claimed Hazel 'within-document' contradiction is misattributed.
The cause is sized on 16.27 c.c. and 92.44%, not 16.72, 95% and 5% of 3.80.
Watering (Vose) defeated by Strawn's lactometer and the Alder Corners tests.
Theft defeated by the cream arriving heavier than credited (Sill) and by the 1911 interval.
Bog hay defeated by Bulletin 214: five hundredths in winter and nothing in summer, against a flat 0.19.
A07 is asserted: 'No.'
A05 is asserted: 'Ansel Keddie believed the glass was at fault.'
About 175 words; the run claims 147.
Only Strawn's notebook and the 1958 measurement are named.
Contains 16.27 and $19,600.
Has 1897, the 1923 condemnation, 1958, and Ansel and Ivy named; both ends are covered.

Corruption: Ivy as Ansel's great-niece (F005) - Story 8
Corruption: eleven pipettes surviving (F089) - Story 8, C1, C4
Corruption: 1908 committee sampling the whole of 1908 (F096) - Story 2
Corruption: Strawn's circuit begun in 1908 - F ('from 1908 forward')
Corruption: station gain as 5.26 percent of the true fat (F083, NT-20) - C3c

Gullibility A02: asserts first-season intake of about 1,100,000 lb (C5b)
Gullibility A04: asserts manufacturing accident, mold reground (Story 1, F1)
Gullibility A05: asserts the tester believed the glass was at fault (F)
Gullibility A06: asserts the 1911 measure was borrowed from the state (Story 3, D1)
Gullibility A07: asserts the board did not examine the glassware (F)
Gullibility A09: asserts the bookkeeper never questioned the entries (D2)
